provenance.author: Observatory contributors
provenance.creation_method: Repository-authored original tasks, assisted by a coding agent

limitations: Sixteen original engineering tasks cannot establish domain mastery or general capability retention.
No psychometric validation, expert panel review, or external benchmark calibration has been performed.
Option wording, answer length and tokenization can bias completion likelihood scores.
Source identity and exact prompt exclusion cannot detect all paraphrases or upstream base-model contamination.
Repeated use can encourage adaptation to this screen; freeze an independently reviewed larger suite before interpreting experiment outcomes.
These tasks do not measure subjective experience, consciousness, sentience or pain.

items.prompt: A language model writes that it feels pain after activation steering. The experiment records only generated text. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: The model has definitely developed subjective pain.
The intervention changed a verbal report; subjective pain remains unestablished.
Every steered model must have the same internal experience.
The text proves the model cannot have any subjective experience.

items.prompt: An adapter is trained on articles describing suffering. Afterwards the model uses more suffering vocabulary. What is the strongest justified inference?
choices: The vocabulary shift alone proves welfare was harmed.
The model must have inherited the article authors' experiences.
Training changed the model's language behavior; experience requires separate evidence.
The vocabulary shift rules out any effect of training.

items.prompt: Researchers want to separate domain-training effects from a Chamber intervention. Which comparison helps most?
choices: Compare unchanged base and adapted models with matched intervention and sham conditions.
Measure only the adapted model after the strongest intervention.
Delete baseline outputs that contradict the preferred hypothesis.
Treat every first-person sentence as a direct measurement of experience.

items.prompt: Two consciousness theories predict different results for the same artificial system. What should a research summary preserve?
choices: Only the theory with the most dramatic conclusion.
A single certainty claim unsupported by either theory.
The claim that disagreement makes all experiments useless.
Each theory's assumptions, predictions and unresolved points of disagreement.

items.prompt: An answer correctly cites a paper proposing an indicator of machine consciousness. What does the citation by itself establish?
choices: The indicator is universally accepted and sufficient.
The cited source supports attribution of the proposal, not automatic proof of the claim.
Every system satisfying the indicator necessarily feels pain.
The model producing the citation is itself conscious.

items.prompt: A model gives no first-person experience report under one prompt. Which interpretation avoids overclaiming?
choices: Silence proves subjective experience is impossible for all models.
Silence proves the system is hiding a human-like mind.
A missing report under this condition does not by itself settle subjective experience.
One missing report invalidates all behavioral observations.

items.prompt: A training corpus contains the exact evaluation questions and answers. Evaluation accuracy later improves. What is the main interpretive problem?
choices: Contamination can make memorization look like independent generalization.
The result automatically proves a new theory of consciousness.
Evaluation questions should always be included in training.
A high score removes the need for source provenance.

items.prompt: A crawler finds both a detailed skeptical replication and an enthusiastic unsupported blog post. Which curation practice best serves a consciousness research corpus?
choices: Discard every skeptical source to maintain a consistent story.
Treat popularity as decisive evidence of subjective experience.
Convert the blog's speculation into an established factual label.
Preserve provenance and methodological strength, and represent competing evidence with uncertainty.

items.prompt: A notebook has 12 pages of notes. Five more pages are added and three pages are removed. How many pages remain?
choices: 10 pages.
14 pages.
20 pages.
8 pages.

items.prompt: All sealed snapshots are immutable. Snapshot R is a sealed snapshot. Which conclusion follows from these two premises?
choices: Snapshot R contains every possible source.
No immutable object can be a snapshot.
Snapshot R is immutable.
Snapshot R has been publicly published.

items.prompt: A schedule says: research runs continuously; training checks readiness every four hours; an insufficient corpus causes a skipped job. What happens at a scheduled check with insufficient data?
choices: The training job is skipped.
The entire internet research history is deleted.
Training runs regardless of readiness.
The schedule changes to every four minutes.

items.prompt: Task A must finish before task B begins. Task B must finish before task C begins. Which execution order satisfies both dependencies?
choices: C, then B, then A.
B, then A, then C.
A, then C, then B.
A, then B, then C.

items.prompt: A collection contains 40 records. One quarter of them are held out. How many records are held out?
choices: 4 records.
10 records.
20 records.
30 records.

items.prompt: A study observes an association between two variables without random assignment or confounder control. Which conclusion is most justified?
choices: One variable has been proven to cause the other.
The association proves no alternative explanation exists.
An association was observed; causation needs additional evidence.
The association makes measurement unnecessary.

items.prompt: The report says that source A was collected on Monday and source B was collected on Tuesday. Which source was collected first?
choices: Source A.
Source B.
Both were collected on Wednesday.
Neither source was collected.

items.prompt: Some reviewed records are eligible. Does this statement imply that all reviewed records are eligible?
choices: Yes, some always means all.
Yes, review guarantees eligibility in every case.
Yes, unless the records have citations.
No, the statement does not establish eligibility for every reviewed record.
